standard_prerequisites.name: Lambda definability
standard_prerequisites.statement: An n-ary number-theoretic function f is lambda definable when there is a lambda term H such that for all n-tuples, H applied to the Church numerals of the arguments beta-reduces to the Church numeral of the value.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the criterion the displayed terms must meet (1100-1108).

standard_prerequisites.name: Church numerals
standard_prerequisites.statement: The Church numeral for n is the term applying its first argument n times to its second argument.
standard_prerequisites.use: The displayed Succ and projection terms act on Church numerals by iteration (1100-1108).

core_obligations: Zero is lambda defined by the term returning the numeral of 0 regardless of its argument (1101-1102).
Succ is lambda defined by the term applying f once more than its numeral argument does (1103-1104).
Each projection is lambda defined by the term returning its i-th argument (1105-1106).
difficulty_reason: The counted lemma is the author lemma at source lines 1094-1098: the zero function, the successor function, and the projections are lambda definable. The author proof (1100-1108) exhibits the defining lambda terms explicitly: Zero as the constant-returning abstraction, Succ as the Church predecessor-plus-one term, and each projection as the abstraction selecting its i-th argument. Each displayed term's defining reduction is the immediate canonical beta-reduction on Church numerals (for Succ: f applied to a f x iterates f once more than a does), so the exhibition of the terms completes the proof by the unit's definition of lambda definability; no verification is deferred to an exercise and no argument is omitted.
